courses.title: Learn the Code
courses.tagline: How this portfolio was built, change by change
courses.blurb: React, Tailwind, animations, canvas effects, performance, the AI chat, deploying through Cloudflare, the Android app, and how Python was made to run in this Learning Lab, explained from zero with the real code and playgrounds.
courses.audience: Anyone curious how a modern website is built, with no coding experience needed.
courses.needs: Nothing. Every term is explained as you go.
outcomes: Read and change the site's code with confidence
Explain React, Tailwind, canvas animation and deployment
Know how the AI chat and in-browser Python work

start.intro: This course explains how this very website was built, one change at a time, for someone who has never coded. You will not write a program here. Instead, every idea comes with a small playground to click, drag and break, and many steps send you to look at the real site.
need: No coding experience and nothing to install.
About 10 minutes for each lesson.
A computer is best for a few steps that look at the page source or resize the window; everything else works on a phone.
order: Start with "From one HTML file to a React app" for the big picture.
Then go module by module: Foundations, Look & feel, The effects, Speed & devices, Features, Shipping it.
The last two modules explain the Learning Lab itself: Python in the browser, then accounts and payments.
"What changed, in order", at the bottom of this page, is the timeline of every change the lessons describe.
lesson: Learn the words
Each lesson starts with its keywords, a plain-English meaning for each, and an everyday comparison. Read them first.
See how it works
A short numbered list shows what happens, in order, for the idea being taught.
Read and try
Short explanations with live examples. Try every one, change something, and see what happens.
Do it yourself, step by step
A numbered walkthrough using the lesson's own playground or the live site: one small action per step, and what you should see. Tick each step as you go.
Practise
Small tasks to try alone, where the lesson has them. A hint is always available.
Pass the quiz
A few questions to check the idea has landed. When the exercises and quiz are right, the lesson is marked complete.
start.tip: Every lesson has a checklist at the top called "Your path through this lesson". Follow it from step 1 and you will never wonder what to do next.

courses.title: Python
courses.tagline: From your first print() to decorators and a real project
courses.blurb: Learn Python by writing it. Every lesson has examples you can edit and run in the browser, exercises that are checked by tests, and a quiz. Examples use collections and finance data, so the skills transfer straight to work.
courses.audience: Complete beginners, and Excel users who want to automate their work.
courses.needs: Nothing. Start at lesson 1 and run every example.
outcomes: Write Python programs with variables, loops, functions and classes
Read and write files, CSV and JSON
Test your code and structure a small project

start.intro: New to coding? This page tells you exactly what to do, in order. You do not need to install anything or know any maths beyond adding and dividing. Go slowly, type everything yourself, and expect to see errors: they are part of learning, not a sign you are doing it wrong.
need: A phone, tablet or computer with a web browser. A keyboard makes typing code easier, but it is not required.
About 20 to 30 minutes for each lesson. One lesson a day is a good pace.
No installs and no account for the first module: Python runs inside this page.
The first time you press Run, Python takes a few seconds to load. After that it is quick.
order: Open lesson 1, "Hello, Python", and finish it before moving on. Each lesson uses what the one before taught.
Work through the modules from top to bottom: Getting started, then Decisions and loops, then Collections.
Stuck on a word? Every keyword is defined at the top of its lesson, and all of them are in the Glossary.
Finished a lesson? The next one is linked at the bottom of the page.
lesson: Learn the words
Each lesson starts with its keywords, a plain-English meaning for each, and an everyday comparison. Read them first.
See how it works
A short numbered list shows what Python does, in order, for the idea being taught.
Read and run
Short explanations with code boxes. Press Run on every one, change a number or a word, and run it again to see what changes.
Do it yourself, step by step
A numbered walkthrough in a practice box: one small action per step, exactly what to type, and what you should see. Tick each step as you go.
Solve the exercises
Small tasks checked automatically. A hint is always available, and the solution if you are truly stuck.
Pass the quiz
A few questions to check the idea has landed. When the exercises and quiz are right, the lesson is marked complete.
start.tip: Every lesson has a checklist at the top called "Your path through this lesson". Follow it from step 1 and you will never wonder what to do next.

courses.blurb: NumPy foundations, then the pandas skills analyst roles ask for most: reading and exploring, selecting, cleaning, groupby, pivot tables, merges and time series, ending in a monthly portfolio report. Best after Python modules 1–4. Loads pandas (about 8 MB) the first time.

start.intro: This course turns the things you already do in Excel (open, filter, sort, SUMIF, VLOOKUP, pivot) into short lines of Python. Every example uses the same made-up collections data, so you always know what you are looking at. Type the code yourself and read each result before moving on.
need: The first four modules of the Python course, up to functions. If print(), variables, lists and loops feel familiar, you are ready.
Nothing to install: pandas runs inside this page. The first Run in a lesson takes a few seconds while pandas loads.
About 30 minutes for each lesson.
Excel experience helps, because each idea is compared with the Excel way of doing it.
order: Start with "From Excel to pandas". It shows the whole course in miniature.
Then the two NumPy lessons: pandas is built on them, and they are short.
Then work down the modules in order: DataFrames, selecting, cleaning, grouping, combining.
Finish with the project, which uses everything once more on raw files.

courses.title: SQL with Python
courses.tagline: The skill analyst job postings ask for most, on a real database
courses.blurb: Write real SQL against a SQLite database of collections data: SELECT and GROUP BY, JOINs, safe parameters and transactions, CTEs and window functions, then hand results to pandas. Best after Python modules 1–4.
courses.audience: Anyone who needs data from a database, the most-requested skill in analyst roles.
courses.needs: Python lessons 1–6 help but are not required for the SQL itself.
outcomes: Write SELECT, GROUP BY and JOIN queries
Change data safely with parameters and transactions
Use window functions and move results into pandas

start.intro: SQL is how you ask a database for exactly the rows you want. Here you write real SQL against a small practice database of accounts and payments that is rebuilt on every Run, so nothing you do can break it. Read each query out loud in plain words before you run it.
need: Nothing to install: the database runs inside this page.
The first six Python lessons help, because queries are sent from a few lines of Python, but you can follow the SQL without them.
About 30 minutes for each lesson.
Type SQL keywords in capitals (SELECT, FROM, WHERE). It is not required, but it makes queries much easier to read.
order: Start with "Databases, tables and rows" to learn what a table is.
Then "Your first queries" and "Aggregates, GROUP BY and CASE": most everyday SQL is in these two.
Then JOINs, and changing data safely.
Finish with window functions and using SQL together with pandas.

start.intro: Kubernetes runs apps across many machines and keeps them running. Real clusters cost money and take time to set up, so this course gives you a simulated three-machine cluster inside the page. The commands and files are the real ones; you just cannot break anything.
need: Nothing to install: the practice cluster runs inside this page.

order: Start with "Containers and why Kubernetes" to meet the cluster.
Then Pods, then Deployments: the two ideas everything else rests on.
Then Services, configuration, and rolling updates.
Finish with the project, which deploys the portfolio from one file.

courses.title: Cloudflare & Web Security

courses.blurb: DNS and nameservers, Cloudflare as a reverse proxy, caching and HTTPS at the edge, robots.txt and blocking AI crawlers without losing search, secret keys, and a public form that sends email without being abused. Taught on this site's real setup.
courses.audience: Anyone who runs or helps run a website: owners, analysts, product people and new developers.

Block AI training crawlers without losing search
Keep secret keys off a website and protect a public form

start.intro: This course explains how shivam-soni.com is delivered and protected, using its real setup: the DNS records, the response headers, robots.txt, the Cloudflare bot rules and the function behind the "Get Resume" form. Every playground uses values taken from the live site.
need: No coding experience and nothing to install.
About 12 minutes for each lesson.
Optional: a terminal for the curl and dig steps (built into macOS and Linux; on Windows use PowerShell or skip them).
order: Start with "How a visit reaches the site": everything else builds on the proxy idea.
Then caching and headers, so you can read what Cloudflare is doing.
Module 2 covers crawlers: first asking politely, then enforcing at the edge.
Module 3 covers secret keys and a public form that sends email safely.
